meta.title: The Smallest Country on Earth Is Smaller Than Most Parks
meta._convention: One scene-spec JSON per script, saved alongside it as <script-name>.scenes.json. Each beat's `duration` is intentionally omitted here -- build_video.js fills it in at render time from the ACTUAL measured length of that beat's generated narration WAV.
meta._note_no_highlight: Vatican City (VA) is a real ISO code but is NOT present as a polygon in world-atlas's 110m-resolution countries topology (too small to survive that simplification, like several other micro-states) -- confirmed empirically against node_modules/world-atlas/countries-110m.json. Treated like the README's 'scenes that aren't a country' pattern: highlight is left empty and a hand-drawn small rectangle in `lines` (approximating VA's real ~44-hectare footprint) stands in for the border outline, using the same gold lineColor as the highlight stroke.

beats.voText: This entire country is 0.17 square miles. You could walk across the whole thing, border to border, in about fifteen minutes.
This is Vatican City, the smallest sovereign state on Earth, sitting entirely inside the city of Rome, surrounded on every side by Italy.
Fewer than 1,000 people live there, and yet it has its own train station, its own postal service, and its own postage stamps.
beats.onScreenText: Its own trains. Its own stamps.

beats.voText: It even has its own army: the Swiss Guard, founded in 1506, the oldest continuously operating military unit anywhere in the world.
Despite the size, it's a fully sovereign nation, recognized around the world, a real country, with real borders, smaller than most parking lots.
One square-ish block, one entire country, one army older than most nations themselves. Follow for more places on Earth that shouldn't exist, but do.
